standard: Maintained experiments must make design provenance, bounded acceptance criteria, outcome, reproducibility, and exact revision-bound evidence explicit.

entries.question: Can Overcenter claim real work and deliver a self-contained byte-complete assignment to an empty disposable worker?
entries.claim: For the bounded proof workload, the claimed Work snapshot plus exact task bytes is sufficient for a no-checkout, no-network worker to produce candidate output that trusted authority can independently settle.
entries.contrast: Assign exact identity but require the worker to obtain source/input bytes through an ambient checkout or mount.
environment: Node.js from .node-version for the deterministic contract.
GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04 for the no-checkout worker and isolated network namespace.
success_criteria: A production SQLite kernel derives READY work and claims it at an exact revision.
The worker receives the claimed Work snapshot and all task-specific bytes in one immutable capsule.
The worker executes with no checkout, repository permission, execution capability, or outbound network namespace.
Missing or altered required bytes fail closed before execution.
Candidate bytes bind to the exact assignment digest, obligation, run, and claimed revision.
Trusted reconstruction and independent observation settle the same run DONE.

artifacts: GitHub Actions run 35488740731: exact-head hosted assignment capsule proof; deterministic contract, no-checkout worker, isolated network namespace, damaged-assignment controls, and trusted settlement all passed.

entries.interpretation: A positive result proves byte-complete assignment plumbing for the bounded workload; it does not make the worker authoritative for success or imply arbitrary toolchain portability.
non_claims: The Node runtime or Linux kernel are embedded in the assignment.
This is a general artifact distribution or confidential payload service.
Arbitrary provider mutation is authorized by the worker capsule.
Every future obligation already fits this proof packet.

design.note: The boundary and fail-closed criteria were committed on the experiment branch before the hosted proof result; later exact-head runs confirm the same bounded contract.

outcome.summary: Exact claimed work and task bytes were delivered to a no-checkout, no-network worker and independently settled by trusted authority.

entries.question: Can Overcenter delegate implementation judgment to a disposable Codex worker while retaining claim, verification, settlement, publication, and readback authority outside the worker?
entries.claim: For the bounded witness, an exact claimed obligation can pass through an untrusted Codex implementation step and become an independently verified, settled, exact-byte draft PR without granting the worker publication authority.
entries.contrast: Let the reasoning worker hold repository write credentials, publish its own patch, or declare its own success.
environment: Node.js from .node-version for the deterministic contract and Overcenter authority steps.
GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04 for the hosted transaction.
OPENAI_API_KEY GitHub Actions secret.
openai/codex-action pinned to 86365089eb2b84e0a8fb0717b304f8bdcb13b20e.
success_criteria: Overcenter derives and claims the witness obligation before the reasoning worker runs.
The Codex job has repository read permission only, no persisted checkout credential, and cannot write Git metadata.
Candidate bytes are confined to the declared path and bound to the exact assignment digest and claimed run.
Trusted reconstruction independently verifies the postcondition and settles the original run DONE.
Only a separate trusted publisher receives repository and pull-request write authority.
GitHub readback reports the exact trusted-publisher commit on the expected base as an open draft PR.

artifacts: .github/workflows/codex-closed-loop.yml
evidence.pending_reason: The deterministic boundary is implemented, but accepted hosted Codex execution evidence under the maintained integration path has not yet been recorded.

entries.interpretation: A positive result establishes the bounded reasoning-worker transaction boundary. It supports using Codex as a disposable implementation worker, not as authority for project truth or provider mutation.
non_claims: Arbitrary code changes are independently verifiable with this one-file witness policy.
Ambiguous GitHub mutation outcomes are recovered automatically.
The worker is trusted because the candidate passed.
GitHub itself is authoritative project state.
The witness pull request should be merged.

design.note: The worker/trusted-authority boundary and acceptance criteria are recorded while the hosted closed-loop outcome remains pending.

outcome.summary: The deterministic contract is maintained, but the hosted reasoning-worker transaction has not yet produced accepted evidence under the current integration boundary.

entries.question: Can a fresh worker recover after the original worker disappears?
entries.claim: Exact durable authority is sufficient for fresh-worker reconstruction and settlement.
entries.contrast: Recovery from worker-local state.
environment: Node.js from .node-version and Git for the deterministic handoff proof.
GitHub Actions for the hosted worker-destruction/provider-readback proof with job-level permission separation.
success_criteria: After the original worker sandbox is destroyed, a fresh worker reconstructs the unresolved run from durable authority without using the original checkout, cache, database, refs, or process memory.
Recovery rotates execution authority so stale execution generation cannot continue acting for the run.
Verifier or obligation replacement is rejected rather than being accepted as recovery of the original claim.
Lost settlement acknowledgement is reconciled without producing a second semantic result.
Missing or ambiguous authority fails closed, and competing authority updates preserve a single CAS winner.
The hosted path settles from independent GitHub readback through the production status-effect boundary rather than trusting the original worker's success assertion.

artifacts: GitHub Actions run 35463403293

entries.interpretation: The experiment demonstrates that run identity and recovery state can survive total worker loss when authority, execution generation, reservation, and receipt identity are durable and independently reconstructible.
non_claims: Every execution substrate physically separates worker and provider credentials.
GitHub repository-scoped statuses:write is coordinate-scoped least privilege.
Fresh recovery is guaranteed to regain liveness.
Worker disposability makes worker assertions authoritative for settlement.

design.note: The original experiment had produced results before the repository-wide experiment contract was introduced. The maintained criteria document the bounded evidence and are not represented as preregistered.

outcome.summary: A fresh worker can reconstruct and settle the same unresolved run from durable authority after the original worker disappears.

entries.question: Can a worker receive exactly declared GitHub bytes without a checkout or repository credential?
entries.claim: Manifest-bound bytes plus permission-separated publication make task scope and result readback independently checkable.
entries.contrast: Give the worker a normal checkout and trust path discipline.
environment: Node.js from .node-version for the deterministic manifest/path contract.
GitHub Actions for permission-separated materialization, no-checkout execution, trusted publication, and authoritative readback.
success_criteria: The deterministic contract accepts only declared GitHub object inputs and bounded writable paths represented by the manifest.
The disposable worker operates from materialized declared blobs without a repository checkout or repository credential.
The worker validates the realized workspace against the same exact manifest bytes it received as read-only input.
Only the trusted publication stage receives repository write authority and publishes the authorized candidate bytes.
Authoritative GitHub readback confirms the published result independently of the worker's local claim.

artifacts: GitHub Actions run 35465653729: materialize, no-checkout execute, publish, and authoritative readback all passed.

entries.interpretation: The hosted proof makes task input identity, writable scope, publication authority, and result readback independently checkable without giving the disposable worker a normal credentialed checkout.
non_claims: The transport is an arbitrary filesystem sandbox.
GitHub provides provider-native coordinate-scoped authorization for the worker.
The manifest proves arbitrary task closure or toolchain completeness.
A worker's candidate output becomes project truth without trusted publication and readback.

design.note: The original experiment had produced results before the repository-wide experiment contract was introduced. The maintained criteria document the bounded evidence and are not represented as preregistered.

outcome.summary: Manifest-bound bytes, no-checkout execution, permission-separated publication, and independent readback make the bounded worker transport independently checkable.

entries.question: Can GitHub read semantics use a schema-derived observation grammar plus explicit semantic projections?
entries.claim: Pinned structural contracts plus semantic projections cover the tested GitHub readback shapes.
entries.contrast: Hand-wire endpoint response assumptions.
environment: Node.js from .node-version.
The deterministic contract uses the repository-pinned GitHub OpenAPI structure for consumed response slices.
GitHub Actions and live GitHub read access for the hosted observation proof.
success_criteria: Consumed GitHub response slices must satisfy the pinned structural contract before semantic projection.
Provider-specific semantic projections assign the tested identity and readback meaning explicitly rather than inheriting meaning from schema structure alone.
Structural drift or malformed consumed fields fail the deterministic observation contract instead of being silently accepted.
The hosted proof exercises the generated observation grammar against live GitHub data at the exact evaluated revision.

artifacts: GitHub Actions run 35463403282

entries.interpretation: The experiment separates structural legality from semantic meaning: generated schema-derived vocabulary constrains legal response shape, while explicit trusted projections continue to define provider identity and readback semantics.
non_claims: The generated grammar covers the entire GitHub API.
OpenAPI structural validity proves that GitHub's returned facts are semantically truthful.
Every GitHub endpoint can share one semantic projection.
Schema generation replaces provider-specific verification logic.

design.note: The original experiment had produced results before the repository-wide experiment contract was introduced. The maintained criteria document the bounded evidence and are not represented as preregistered.

outcome.summary: Schema-derived structural legality plus explicit semantic projection covers the tested GitHub observation slices without conflating shape with meaning.

entries.question: Can Overcenter maintain a reproducible total ordering of production-code importance from quantitative facts?
entries.claim: A revision-bound callable graph plus explicit authority/recovery semantics can derive an inspectable production-code criticality vector and a calibrated total order without ranking tests or experiments themselves.
entries.contrast: Periodically repeat a human ranking exercise or rely on generic complexity/hotspot metrics alone.
environment: Node.js from .node-version
Git with full repository history for revision-bound blame/change exposure
TypeScript 5.8.3 installed for the analyzer
success_criteria: Only production callables under src/ enter the ranked population.
Configured authority and recovery selectors resolve exactly once.
Internal static-call resolution remains informative; unresolved internal/unknown calls are reported, and critical callback-boundary exemptions fail closed when stale or malformed.
Every named required calibration regression remains satisfied while known model mismatches remain explicit diagnostics rather than consuming a percentage budget.
Every surprising rank decomposes into quantitative vector components and graph evidence.
Deleting generated reports and recomputing at the same revision produces the same result.

artifacts: GitHub Actions run 35673456200: production criticality ranking passed after component-local normalization made unchanged authority components invariant to disconnected production code.
experiments/production-criticality-ranking/mutation-evidence.json: exact-blob-bound hostile-case evidence; stale probes fail closed to a full evidence gap.

entries.interpretation: The maintained ranking provides reproducible consequence and engineering-attention orders from revision-bound graph and evidence facts. Component-local normalization prevents unrelated disconnected code from perturbing unchanged authority components. Required calibration regressions remain explicit, branch-level/callable-granularity mismatches remain diagnostics, and mutation evidence is exact-blob-bound so stale probes fail closed rather than silently transferring.
non_claims: Callable boundaries are the final semantic unit.
Static test reachability is equivalent to hostile-case evidence.
Exported-entrypoint reachability is equivalent to production telemetry.
The current weighting equation is uniquely correct.

design.note: Prior human pairwise judgments predate the analyzer, but callable granularity, ranking policy, component normalization, and mutation-evidence handling evolved in response to observed disagreements and gaps.

outcome.summary: The ranking is reproducible and useful for consequence/attention ordering, while callable granularity and hostile-case evidence remain explicit model limitations rather than hidden calibration errors.

entries.question: For one successful production GitHub status transaction, how much latency belongs to Overcenter local correctness machinery versus provider I/O?
entries.claim: The benchmark separates SQLite authority, reservation, provider identity, the mutation boundary, readback, and local settlement costs while exercising the unchanged production GitHub status effect.
entries.contrast: Infer feasibility from whole GitHub Actions job duration or storage microbenchmarks without timing the production transaction boundary.
environment: Node.js from .node-version.
Local mode uses SQLite plus an in-memory fake GitHub transport.
Hosted live mode uses GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04 and the workflow GITHUB_TOKEN with statuses: write.
success_criteria: Every sample claims exact SQLite-backed work and settles DONE from authoritative readback.
Experiment-only timing wraps the production effect boundary without changing production mutation code.
Provider-facing I/O and local Overcenter work are reported separately.

artifacts: GitHub Actions run 35540143115: 25-sample deterministic baseline and 3-sample live GitHub decomposition passed with production source unchanged.
experiments/production-latency/results/2026-09-20.md

entries.interpretation: Use the result as a single-operation latency decomposition. Compare provider and Overcenter-local cost; do not extrapolate it directly to concurrency or large-history throughput.
non_claims: Large-history projection remains constant-time.
SQLite is a distributed or HA authority store.
GitHub rate limits permit arbitrary transaction throughput.
Recovery-path latency matches successful-path latency.
Other providers have the same latency profile.

design.note: The transaction boundary and timing buckets were fixed for the hosted measurement, while the numeric latency result is observational rather than a preregistered performance threshold.

outcome.summary: The benchmark separates Overcenter-local correctness work from provider-facing latency for the bounded successful GitHub status transaction.

analysis.estimand: Observed successful single-transaction latency decomposition on the exact hosted GitHub treatment.

uncertainty.reason: The evaluated live result contains only three samples and is intentionally descriptive rather than a population latency estimate.

analysis.stopping_rule: The historical evaluated treatment used exactly three live GitHub samples.

entries.question: Does the production runCoreLoop bounded-concurrency path recover useful parallel throughput while one kernel retains all execution authority and settlement responsibility?
entries.claim: The benchmark measures the production core loop at concurrency 1, 2, 4, and 8 across 0, 25, and 100 ms effect costs while checking that only packet-level effects overlap and observed overlap never exceeds the configured bound.
entries.contrast: Infer production scaling from a hand-built concurrency harness instead of measuring the core-loop API that would ship.

design.note: The workload descends from the earlier bounded-concurrency treatment. The 15-round paired sampling plan, counterbalanced order, bootstrap interval, fixed stopping rule, and 2.0x lower-bound decision criterion were committed before the exact-head confirmatory run.

outcome.summary: The preregistered fixed-N paired treatment cleared the 2.0x lower-confidence-bound criterion at both material effect costs while the zero-cost negative control remained near 1x.

environment: Node.js from .node-version.
Local filesystem supporting SQLite.
Hosted reference uses GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04.
success_criteria: All 32 obligations settle DONE through production runCoreLoop for every case.
Reported max_active_effects never exceeds requested concurrency.
For both 25 ms and 100 ms artificial effect cost, the concurrency-8 median paired throughput ratio has a 95% bootstrap lower bound greater than 2.0x versus concurrency 1.
Only packet-level effects overlap; exact claims, reservations, observation, and settlement remain kernel-owned.

artifacts: GitHub Actions Core-loop bounded concurrency run 36084917077: exact-head 15-round counterbalanced paired treatment passed.
25 ms effects: concurrency 8 median paired speedup 3.181x, 95% percentile-bootstrap interval [3.150x, 3.289x], median throughput 92.662 tasks/s versus 29.155 at concurrency 1.
100 ms effects: concurrency 8 median paired speedup 5.594x, 95% percentile-bootstrap interval [5.463x, 5.675x], median throughput 51.849 tasks/s versus 9.255 at concurrency 1.
0 ms negative control: concurrency 8 median paired speedup 1.002x with 95% interval [0.677x, 1.036x]; max_active_effects remained 1.

entries.interpretation: On the exact hosted treatment, bounded packet-level effect concurrency behind one serialized authority lane produced a statistically separated material speedup when effect cost was nontrivial. The zero-cost control remained consistent with no throughput benefit, so concurrency acts as latency hiding rather than a universal multiplier.
non_claims: Artificial delay models a particular provider.
SQLite is distributed or highly available.
Fairness is proved by the performance benchmark.
Zero-cost work benefits from additional effect concurrency.
Evidence-only commits after the evaluated treatment revision change the measured result.

analysis.estimand: Median within-round throughput ratio for concurrency 8 relative to concurrency 1, separately at 25 ms and 100 ms artificial effect cost.

sampling.order: alternate forward and reverse concurrency order each round

analysis.stopping_rule: Collect exactly 15 paired rounds per effect cost; do not stop early on observed speedup.
analysis.decision_rule: Support material bounded-concurrency speedup only when the lower 95% bootstrap bound exceeds 2.0x for concurrency 8 at both 25 ms and 100 ms effect cost.

entries.question: Can Rust preserve the current GitHub commit-status mutation admission semantics while making weaker authority impossible to pass to the effect primitive through safe code without materially reducing local admission performance?
entries.claim: A sealed, affine, zero-sized Rust execution capability can preserve the modeled production admission decision exactly while making raw, forged, and reused authority invalid at compile time with no more than a 10% median local admission regression.
entries.contrast: Keep the current structural execution permit plus repeated runtime proof obligations at downstream effect call sites.
environment: Stable Rust compiler on Linux x86-64 for the hosted measurement.
Optimized rustc -O build with std::hint::black_box around benchmark inputs.
No network, provider credential, SQLite store, or external service is required for the modeled authority differential.
Host CPU scheduling affects absolute timing, so the benchmark alternates baseline/treatment rounds and compares medians within one process.
success_criteria: All 131,072 modeled authority combinations produce the same admission or error class in the structural baseline and typed treatment.
Only the fully valid authority tuple crosses the modeled effect boundary.
Raw authority invocation, safe capability forgery, and reuse of a consumed capability each fail compilation for the intended type-system reason.
ExecutionPermit<GithubCommitStatus> is zero-sized and requires no drop glue.
Median optimized sequential typed admission is no more than 1.10x the structural baseline.
Median optimized concurrent typed admission is no more than 1.10x the structural baseline.

artifacts: GitHub Actions run 35819335382, job 107047627325: typed capability authority experiment PASS.
131,071 hostile authority combinations plus valid control matched baseline admission exactly.
Sequential median ratio 0.949x; concurrent 4-thread median ratio 0.959x; both below preregistered 1.10x ceiling.

entries.interpretation: A passing result would justify testing the same capability representation at an actual Rust-owned mutation boundary; it would not by itself justify moving durable authority, provider observation, settlement, or graph semantics out of the TypeScript + SQLite production path.
non_claims: Runtime generation, revision, lifecycle, unresolved-effect, or provider-contract checks can be removed from the authoritative ingress.
A capability remains valid after external authority changes without revalidation or an atomic fence.
Provider credentials become coordinate-scoped or least-privilege because the local Rust type is effect-specific.
The modeled local admission benchmark proves end-to-end transaction latency or distributed throughput.
Rust should replace the current TypeScript + SQLite authority implementation.
Safe Rust types defend against unsafe code, process compromise, or a malicious trusted provider adapter.

design.note: Question, hostile-state corpus, compile-fail controls, and 1.10x sequential/concurrent performance thresholds were recorded before the first hosted experiment run.

outcome.summary: At exact revision 637d15c0f7d29cf0aec9be6afc9cfc40a8d0ea06, the typed Rust capability matched the modeled production admission decision across all 131,072 cases, rejected raw/forged/reused authority at compile time, remained zero-sized, and measured 0.949x sequential and 0.959x concurrent median admission time versus the structural baseline.

entries.question: Once execution authority is established, can Overcenter preserve it through the trusted GitHub effect broker instead of repeatedly decomposing it into raw identifiers and reconstructing the same relationship at each provider?
entries.claim: A nominal EffectAuthority minted once at provider ingress can eliminate duplicated provider authority reconstruction, prevent raw ExecutionPermit from reaching performEffect, preserve the independent stale-generation reservation fence, avoid net source growth, and keep same-runner local production latency within 1.10x baseline.
entries.contrast: Each provider independently reconstructs claimed work from a raw ExecutionPermit, rechecks run/revision/effect/verifier fields, and passes the raw permit to performEffect before the current-head reservation fence.

reproduce.local: npm install --ignore-scripts --package-lock=false && npm run test:effect-authority-decay && npm run bench:effect-authority-decay

environment: Node from .node-version and the repository-pinned TypeScript/type definitions in package.json.
Exact current-main baseline 81b350e526824ab2c397642e6761a0c860151331 retained in Git history for source and same-runner latency comparison.
No live provider credentials are required; provider regression uses deterministic fake GitHub I/O.
success_criteria: Raw permit/work mismatch is rejected before provider I/O and before effect reservation.
Authority superseded after binding during provider read I/O is rejected by the unchanged final reservation fence before provider mutation.
The production TypeScript checker rejects a raw ExecutionPermit at performEffect and rejects structural EffectAuthority forgery.
Provider claimedWork calls, raw coordinate comparisons, effect-contract checks, verifier checks, and performEffect(rawPermit) calls all fall to zero, with exactly one centralized authority mint.
Combined nonblank SLOC across engine.ts and the two admitted GitHub effect providers does not increase relative to baseline.
Median-of-run medians for effect_reservation_ms and overcenter_local_ms are each no more than 1.10x the exact baseline on the same hosted runner.
Existing GitHub status and PR update-branch provider effect regressions remain green.

artifacts: GitHub Actions run 35825868462, job 107067328128: production typecheck, adversarial runtime controls, authority-decay census, provider regressions, and same-runner latency differential passed.
Merge-gate run 35825868706, candidate-evidence job 107067329353: repository typecheck and full deterministic regression passed on the same treatment revision.
Provider claimedWork calls 2 -> 0; raw coordinate comparisons 6 -> 0; effect-contract checks 2 -> 0; verifier checks 2 -> 0; provider raw performEffect calls 2 -> 0; one central authority mint.
Combined production SLOC 909 -> 907.
Same-runner effect reservation median 0.718 ms -> 0.726 ms (1.011x); Overcenter local median 4.430 ms -> 4.324 ms (0.976x).
Authority superseded during provider I/O was rejected by the unchanged final beginEffect fence before provider mutation or effect reservation.

entries.interpretation: Typed capabilities pay off where runtime-established authority would otherwise decay into raw data and repeated trusted-interior reconstruction. Preserve historical reconstruction APIs that have distinct semantic jobs, and retain a final runtime fence anywhere external authority can change before the effect.
non_claims: TypeScript nominal branding provides Rust affine or ownership guarantees.
Bound authority remains current after external execution authority changes.
The final current-head reservation fence can be removed.
Provider identity observation or authoritative readback can be skipped.
Wire protocols can trust in-process types instead of validating received data.
Explicit unsafe casts or malicious trusted code are prevented.

design.note: Confirmatory current-main criteria were fixed before this run, but the corrected treatment incorporates lessons from an earlier prototype that exposed legitimate historical reconstruction and low-level reservation consumers.

outcome.summary: On current-main baseline 81b350e526824ab2c397642e6761a0c860151331, bound EffectAuthority removed all duplicated provider authority reconstruction, reduced the measured production slice by 2 nonblank lines, preserved the stale-generation mutation fence, passed repository typecheck and full deterministic regression, and stayed within the 1.10x latency ceiling.

entries.question: Does Overcenter's current durable GitHub commit-status state vocabulary preserve every distinction that matters to retry safety across uncertainty at the provider boundary?
entries.claim: The current effect-reservation, observation, and receipt vocabulary distinguishes materially different mutation-certainty states that require different safe retry decisions.
entries.contrast: A bounded explorer finds two physically different worlds with different retry safety that reconstruct to the same durable Overcenter recovery fingerprint.
environment: Node.js from .node-version.
Production TypeScript GitHub commit-status adapter and production SQLite authority kernel.
Injected provider transport and readback visibility; no network or provider credential is required.
success_criteria: All ten declared reachable uncertainty worlds execute through the real production adapter and SQLite recovery path.
An unresolved reservation blocks every attempted second provider mutation.
DONE occurs only when a matching remote effect is visible to authoritative readback.
The explorer kills retry-on-any-throw, retry-on-RECOVERY_REQUIRED, and trust-HTTP-201-without-readback negative controls.
The preregistered definitely-not-dispatched world and committed-but-readback-hidden world are compared for exact durable recovery equivalence.
The hypothesis is falsified if those two worlds require different physical retry decisions yet produce the same durable recovery fingerprint.

artifacts: GitHub Actions Merge gate run 35822437473, rerun attempt 2, candidate-evidence job 107057254622: exact-head deterministic experiment PASS.
10 reachable provider-boundary worlds collapsed to 2 durable equivalence classes with 1 retry-safety collision.

Preregistered witness: connect-fails-before-dispatch and dispatch-present-throw-hidden both reconstructed to RECOVERY_REQUIRED with COLLECTION_ABSENCE_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE while duplicate retry remained blocked.
All three unsafe negative controls were killed; no production blind retry or false DONE was observed.

The first attempted run at 709b0b5d345744e7aa7e5c8f7e5a45ad6112bf76 was discarded before interpretation because a test-fixture path assertion rejected the production paginated readback request; c4c3564bb02618642fcb9d046686772f7adb8224 fixes only that fixture.

entries.interpretation: A collision is evidence of a liveness/knowledge gap, not a duplicate-effect safety failure: Overcenter may conservatively retain RECOVERY_REQUIRED even when trustworthy pre-dispatch evidence could make retry safe.
non_claims: Arbitrary provider adapters are covered.
Node fetch can always prove that no request bytes were dispatched.
Transport errors or HTTP 502 responses are authoritative absence evidence.
Real GitHub timing or eventual-consistency distributions are measured.
This bounded enumerator is a complete symbolic or concolic executor.

design.note: The uncertainty grammar, preregistered witness pair, durable fingerprint, safety invariants, and three negative controls were recorded before execution. The only post-run harness correction fixed an over-escaped paginated-readback path assertion; it did not change the preregistered experiment semantics.

outcome.summary: At exact revision c4c3564bb02618642fcb9d046686772f7adb8224, a definitely-not-dispatched failure and a committed-but-readback-hidden failure required different physical retry decisions but reconstructed to the same durable RECOVERY_REQUIRED state. The current representation remains safe because unresolved reservations block blind replay, but it loses retry-relevant dispatch knowledge.

entries.question: Can a trusted HTTPS transport boundary produce a NOT_DISPATCHED witness strong enough to distinguish definitely-not-dispatched mutation from an uncertain mutation outcome?
entries.claim: On a fresh HTTPS socket, failure before TLS secureConnect can be retained as NOT_DISPATCHED while every later transport failure remains UNKNOWN.
entries.contrast: Infer dispatch certainty from coarse transport error strings or map all mutation transport failures to one UNKNOWN state.
environment: Node.js from .node-version.
Node https.request using fresh sockets only.
Loopback TCP/TLS peers with a fixed test certificate; no external network or provider credential is required.
success_criteria: DNS failure before connection establishment yields NOT_DISPATCHED.
TLS-handshake reset before secureConnect yields NOT_DISPATCHED and zero peer-observed application bytes.
Reset after secureConnect yields UNKNOWN and the peer observes decrypted HTTP request bytes.
HTTP 201 after receiving the mutation body yields ACKNOWLEDGED.
No world with peer-observed application bytes yields NOT_DISPATCHED.
Error-code-only and any-transport-error NOT_DISPATCHED negative controls are killed.

artifacts: GitHub Actions Merge gate run 35824901839, rerun attempt 2, candidate-evidence job 107064713901: exact-head experiment and candidate proof PASS.
DNS failure: NOT_DISPATCHED, secure_connected=false, peer_application_bytes=0.
TLS-handshake reset: NOT_DISPATCHED, secure_connected=false, ECONNRESET, peer_tls_bytes=349, peer_application_bytes=0.
Post-secureConnect reset: UNKNOWN, secure_connected=true, ECONNRESET, peer_application_bytes=172.
HTTP 201 control: ACKNOWLEDGED, secure_connected=true, peer_application_bytes=48.
Error-code-only and any-transport-error NOT_DISPATCHED negative controls were both killed.
The exact-head gate also passed TypeScript type-checking, TLA+ verification, production computation boundary proof, and self-application.

entries.interpretation: The bounded result supports a narrow transport-phase witness for fresh HTTPS sockets. The next experiment should place this transport beneath the real GitHub commit-status effect and prove that only NOT_DISPATCHED releases replay while UNKNOWN preserves RECOVERY_REQUIRED.
non_claims: Reused keep-alive sockets satisfy the same evidence rule.
HTTP/2, QUIC, proxies, or arbitrary transports expose an equivalent boundary.
secureConnect proves a mutation occurred.
The current production fetch wrapper already exposes this evidence.
Production retry semantics should change before a real-effect-path treatment is tested.

design.note: The fresh-socket secureConnect boundary, four transport worlds, peer-byte oracle, and two unsafe negative controls were committed before first execution.

outcome.summary: At exact revision 0420435e83f4fd66cbeed4f3093b3c97efa78bdb, the fresh-socket HTTPS treatment emitted NOT_DISPATCHED only for failures before TLS secureConnect, kept post-connect failure UNKNOWN when the peer had already observed 172 decrypted HTTP bytes, and returned ACKNOWLEDGED on HTTP 201. No peer-observed application-byte case was misclassified as NOT_DISPATCHED.

entries.question: Can trusted fresh-socket NOT_DISPATCHED evidence release exactly one GitHub commit-status reservation without weakening no-blind-replay?
entries.claim: An exact-run reservation can terminate READY only when current execution authority presents an adapter-admitted NOT_DISPATCHED evidence kind bound to that reservation.
entries.contrast: Leave every reserved transport failure in RECOVERY_REQUIRED, or infer replay safety from coarse transport/HTTP errors.
environment: Node.js from .node-version.
Production GitHub commit-status effect, authority kernel, durable SQLite fact store, and fresh-socket Node HTTPS transport.
Loopback TCP/TLS peers; no external GitHub mutation is required.
success_criteria: Pre-secureConnect TLS failure atomically clears the reservation and terminates the old run READY.
Retry after a trusted release requires a new run and creates a new unresolved reservation until provider readback.
Post-secureConnect failure with peer-observed HTTP bytes retains the reservation and reaches RECOVERY_REQUIRED after interruption.
HTTP 502 retains the reservation.
Forged evidence kind cannot release a reservation.
Stale execution authority cannot release a reservation.
GitHub commit-status provider replay capability remains forbidden.

artifacts: GitHub Actions Merge gate run 35883788255, rerun attempt 2, candidate-evidence job 107259296679: exact-head experiment, TLA+, production computation boundary, and self-application PASS.
Pre-secureConnect failure: peer_tls_bytes=349; old run READY; reservation released; retry used a distinct new run.
Successful retry HTTP 201 left the new run reservation unresolved pending authoritative readback.
Post-secureConnect reset: peer_application_bytes=377; final status RECOVERY_REQUIRED; mutation_replay_posts=0; unresolved effect retained.
HTTP 502: peer_application_bytes=97; unresolved effect retained.
Forged evidence and stale authority were both blocked with the reservation retained.
GitHub commit-status provider replay remained forbidden while reservation release was limited to the admitted trusted-not-dispatched evidence kind.

Standing effect-authority-decay workflow passed runtime authority controls, provider regressions, and same-runner latency after its historical SLOC metric was correctly scoped to its evaluated revision.

entries.interpretation: Support would justify a narrow production liveness improvement: terminate a single attempt READY from trusted pre-dispatch evidence while retaining provider replay as forbidden and keeping unknown outcomes recovery-required.
non_claims: Generic provider replay safety is established.
Reused sockets, proxies, HTTP/2, or QUIC satisfy the same evidence rule.
secureConnect proves provider mutation.
Transport evidence can settle DONE.
Adapters without an explicit reservation-release capability may use this path.

design.note: The atomic release+READY design, four cases, capability separation, and falsification criteria were committed before first execution. The first treatment head was stopped by typechecking because an existing capability test fixture lacked the newly required reservation_release field; that fixture-only repair did not change the preregistered cases. entries.question: Under explicit availability and observation assumptions, does scheduler selection guarantee progress for a continuously eligible recovered obligation, and where does the current fresh-first policy cease to be starvation-free?
entries.claim: A fixed finite READY set should be starvation-free under the production least-recently-claimed selector; deliberately fixed-priority scheduling should admit starvation; and continual admission of never-claimed work is tested as a hostile boundary for the current fresh-first rule.
entries.contrast: Treat throughput or a bounded fixed-set replay test as proof of temporal liveness under all admissible workloads.
entries.interpretation: Exact-head formal and executable evidence agree. The production selector is starvation-free for the tested stable finite set: a preclaimed READY recovery target was selected on claim opportunity 9 with eight initially fresh contenders at simulated concurrency 1, 2, and 4. The deliberately fixed-priority selector starved the target and TLC found the corresponding temporal counterexample. More importantly, continually replenishing the never-claimed class also starved the target under the current production fresh-first selector at all tested concurrency values, and TLC independently found an infinite temporal counterexample. Therefore the broad liveness theorem is false without an additional admission assumption or stronger cross-class fairness.

Overcenter can force unavailable authority or missing provider observations to recover.

A bounded executable starvation trace by itself proves an infinite temporal property; that role belongs to the TLA+ counterexample.

The broader open-system liveness theorem is falsified without an extra admission assumption or stronger cross-class fairness.

entries.question: Which deterministic replay-derived scheduler policy survives recovered-target fresh floods, fresh-target recovery pressure, and adversarial same-class arrivals without adding a mutable scheduler cursor?

entries.interpretation: The bounded result supports authenticated, context-bound capability evidence as an admission representation. outcome.summary: Authenticated evidence admitted only controlled isolation for confinement-sensitive obligations, rejected observed ambient authority, rejected point-in-time absence as execution authority, and passed forgery, schema, scope, issuer-authority, revision, execution, and epoch-context falsifiers.

A candidate produced from an older base integrates over an unrelated main advance and preserves both source changes.
A candidate that changes any undeclared path is rejected before the authoritative target ref moves.
A current-main conflict causes re-realization to be required and leaves the authoritative target ref unchanged.
A cleanly applicable candidate whose current-source acceptance context changed fails acceptance and leaves the authoritative target ref unchanged.
If main advances after verification but before CAS, integration retries from the new head, preserves the concurrent change, and exact replay creates no second integration commit.
A forged integration trailer on an unrelated main commit is not accepted as replay evidence unless trusted reconstruction proves the exact candidate tree and current acceptance.

entries.question: Can Overcenter factor durable project authority into immutable content-addressed fact objects plus a separately linearizable authority-head CAS without changing project semantics?
entries.claim: For the bounded treatment, semantic fact payloads can live in an independently addressed immutable object store while Git stores only one fact-id pointer per authority revision and supplies exact-head CAS. The composed store preserves the DurableFactStore contract, matches the monolithic Git kernel's logical transitions, fails closed when an authoritative fact object is missing, and admits exactly one winner under an eight-process same-head race even though losing immutable objects remain published but unreachable.
entries.contrast: Keep semantic fact payload and serialization authority inseparable inside one monolithic strongly consistent database or Git history.
environment: Node.js from .node-version.
Production DurableFactStore, KernelCore, runCoreLoop, and monolithic GitOvercenterKernel are used for the differential.
The candidate immutable fact store is a SHA-256 content-addressed directory with idempotent create-only writes.
The candidate authority-head service is a Git ref whose commits contain only one fact-id pointer and whose expected-old-value update-ref operation is the serialization point.
Eight child processes share the immutable object directory and authority repository for the same-head contention treatment.
success_criteria: The composed split store satisfies initialize, append, stale-writer rejection, historical replay, reopen, and current-head behavior equivalent to the DurableFactStore contract.
Every reachable authority-head commit tree contains exactly one file named fact-id and no semantic graph, claim, execution-authority, reservation, release, or receipt payload.
A stale append may leave an immutable content object behind, but that orphan is absent from authoritative history and cannot affect project projection.
Eight processes racing one exact expected head produce exactly one authority winner, one authoritative claim, and seven losing immutable fact objects that remain unreachable.
If a fact object referenced by authoritative head history is removed, replay fails closed with FACT_OBJECT_MISSING rather than silently skipping or reconstructing an empty transition.
A fresh replica of the immutable object directory reconstructs byte-equivalent normalized authoritative history through the same authority-head service.

The split-store KernelCore and the monolithic GitOvercenterKernel derive identical normalized project state, explanations, and receipts before and after a two-obligation production core-loop workload.

Eight-process same-head race: 8 contenders, exactly 1 winner, 1 authoritative claim, 9 immutable objects total, and 7 unreachable loser objects.
Merge gate run 35939753680 passed lint, typecheck, experiment contracts, adapter diagnosability, and deterministic regression on the same exact revision.

entries.interpretation: The bounded result supports the decomposition itself: immutable semantic fact publication and project-authority serialization need not share one transaction boundary. The authority-head CAS remained the sole operation deciding project truth, while losing content objects were harmless unreachable garbage and missing referenced objects failed closed. This justifies promoting separate ImmutableFactObjects and AuthorityHead interfaces, not the directory-backed experimental implementation.
non_claims: A directory is an appropriate production distributed object store.
The immutable object store requires no durability, replication, integrity, or availability guarantees.
The authority-head service is consensus-free or highly available merely because its state is small.
Git is the preferred production authority-head implementation.
Garbage collection of unreachable fact objects is safe without a separate publication/retention protocol.
The experiment proves multi-region partition tolerance, Byzantine behavior, or an HA SLA.
Backend-local revision identities become portable or byte-identical across authority-head implementations.

design.note: The split responsibilities, semantic differential, head-payload restriction, missing-object negative control, eight-process same-head race, orphan-object expectation, and replica reconstruction criterion were recorded before first execution.

outcome.summary: At exact revision 7546e2b058c8be80faebaa8900a684b794275af3, the split store matched monolithic Git kernel semantics, kept authority commits fact-id-only, admitted exactly one winner in an eight-process same-head race, left seven losing fact objects unreachable, reconstructed from a copied object replica, and failed closed when an authoritative fact object was missing.

entries.question: Can trusted validation establish authoritative identity for generated artifact bytes that were not known when the obligation was defined, while downstream work consumes only retained evidence and an authoritative settlement receipt?
entries.claim: For the bounded source-proposal model, evidence-first publication plus exact claim binding, trusted scope derivation from artifact bytes, exact-head authority CAS, and settlement-receipt dependency identity is sufficient to represent generated output without trusting a worker-declared digest or predeclaring exact output bytes.
entries.contrast: Treat the worker's declared output identity as authoritative, or append authority before the generated bytes are durably retained.
entries.interpretation: The exact-head treatment supports a narrow verified-generated-output primitive: trusted software may establish post-execution artifact identity from retained bytes, publish that evidence before authority, and let downstream work consume the authoritative settlement receipt. This does not authorize source integration or replace fixed postconditions for ordinary provider effects.
environment: Node.js from .node-version.
Production FileEvidenceStore and EvidenceRef implementation.
One deterministic experimental exact-head authority CAS; no production settlement schema is changed.
Canonical JSON source-proposal artifacts whose changed paths are derived by trusted validation from retained bytes.
No network, provider credential, database, GitHub mutation, LLM, or source integration is required.
success_criteria: A valid generated artifact whose bytes are unknown at definition time is durably published, authority-referenced, read back by EvidenceRef, and yields downstream identity through the authoritative settlement receipt.
Two distinct valid artifact byte sequences under identical claim metadata produce distinct EvidenceRefs, distinct settlement commits, and distinct downstream semantic identities.
Wrong assignment digest, run ID, claimed authority revision, or source revision is rejected before authoritative state changes.
An artifact that writes outside the declared source scope is rejected using paths derived from the artifact bytes rather than worker-declared changed-path metadata.
Evidence publication without authority append leaves authority unchanged and only an orphan immutable object.
Two valid writers from one expected authority head may both publish evidence, but exactly one authority CAS wins and only that settlement determines downstream identity.
Corrupt or missing evidence referenced by an authoritative receipt makes downstream consumption fail closed.
The unsafe worker-declared-output-identity control demonstrates a semantic collision for distinct artifact bytes.
The unsafe authority-first control demonstrates a dangling authoritative reference to unpublished evidence.
non_claims: Arbitrary generated source proposals are semantically correct.
Source integration, merge conflict handling, or Git ref mutation is safe.
Generated outputs should replace fixed postconditions for ordinary provider effects.
The local FileEvidenceStore is a distributed artifact service.
Online garbage collection is safe while evidence publishers are in flight.
A settlement receipt remains usable when its referenced evidence cannot be verified.
A reasoning worker may choose its own claim, source revision, writable scope, verifier, or settlement identity.
Source proposal and source integration must be exposed as two user-visible graph nodes.

design.note: Question, treatment ordering, nine distinguishing cases, negative controls, and promotion boundary were recorded before the first hosted exact-head execution.

outcome.summary: At exact revision 8f58d6d874afaa720d3ecc8a63f0d609e3717eb3, the preregistered treatment supported evidence-backed generated output: distinct valid artifacts produced distinct evidence, settlement, and downstream identities; all four forged claim bindings and the source-scope violation were rejected; evidence-first crash and writer-race cases preserved authority safety; referenced corruption failed closed; and both unsafe negative controls were killed.

entries.question: Can a second provider mutation use the existing semantic-intent, exact claim/fence, durable effect reservation, Kubernetes observation, and settlement machinery without introducing Kubernetes-shaped kernel logic?
entries.claim: An experiment-local ConfigMap ensure broker can reserve before PATCH, fail closed across ambiguous mutation outcomes, and settle from authoritative Kubernetes state using the existing generic kernel and existing LIST/WATCH certificate boundary.
entries.contrast: Add a Kubernetes mutation adapter directly to production and infer provider generality from ordinary success without testing ambiguous outcomes, identity replacement, continuity loss, or retries.
environment: Node.js from .node-version.
Production SQLite authority kernel and production Kubernetes ConfigMap LIST/WATCH certificate implementation.
Experiment-local semantic ensure and PATCH broker; Kubernetes is not added to the production semantic registry or trusted dispatcher.
Deterministic provider harness injects success, timeout-before-commit, timeout-after-commit, resourceVersion conflict, delete/recreate UID change, and broken WATCH continuity.
success_criteria: A successful PATCH is durably reserved before mutation and reaches DONE only after authoritative provider observation.
Timeout after commit reaches RECOVERY_REQUIRED first, then settles DONE from fresh LIST without a second PATCH.
Delete/recreate after an ambiguous commit reports the replacement UID rather than preserving the original UID.
A resourceVersion conflict is not itself settlement evidence; fresh provider state determines whether the semantic ensure is satisfied.
Broken WATCH continuity cannot extend prior absence evidence.
Fresh authoritative absence with an unresolved reservation remains RECOVERY_REQUIRED and an attempted retry issues zero additional PATCHes.
The generic authority engine contains no Kubernetes-specific branch or recovery rule.

entries.interpretation: Support would justify promoting Kubernetes ConfigMap ensure as production provider mutation #2 through EffectAuthority and trusted dispatch while retaining no-blind-replay and provider-neutral kernel semantics.
non_claims: A production Kubernetes credential or RBAC boundary is proven.
Transport-level dispatch certainty against a real API server is proven.
Automatic replay of Kubernetes mutations is safe.
A Kubernetes NOT_DISPATCHED reservation-release rule is established.
ConfigMap data equality, field-manager ownership, or arbitrary Kubernetes resources are covered.
Kubernetes is already a supported production mutation provider.

design.note: The five hostile cases, no-blind-retry condition, and zero-kernel-special-case criterion were fixed before hosted execution. The mutation broker remains experiment-local so a positive result does not silently become production support. The first hosted candidate reached the retry case and was blocked by RUN_NOT_EXECUTING before the expected UNRESOLVED_EFFECT fence; the oracle was widened only to accept either generic pre-provider blocker while retaining the zero-additional-PATCH success criterion.

outcome.summary: At exact revision 1bcce9df74b40875797ac4f1fd4441b578da4f27, all preregistered Kubernetes ConfigMap mutation falsifiers passed using the generic reservation and settlement machinery: ambiguous commit recovered by observation without replay, UID replacement was preserved, resourceVersion conflict deferred to fresh state, stale WATCH absence failed closed, retry performed zero provider mutations, and the kernel required no Kubernetes-specific branch.
